From landing her first holiday job at 17 to becoming the Marketing Manager of Communications Fiji Limited and the owner of The Rotisserie, Felisha Hazelman-Tuiloma has built a career shaped by curiosity, resilience and a willingness to embrace new opportunities.

On this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, Tuiloma opens up about her journey, the lessons that shaped her career and the challenges of balancing family life, running her own business and leading marketing at one of Fiji's leading media organisations.

item.title: Vuna villagers call for action on long-running water problems
item.description: Vuna villager Sulio Batirerega says the community is mainly relying on rainwater, but prolonged dry conditions have made the situation increasingly difficult. He says water tanks have been provided to some residents, but these are only useful when there is enough rain to fill them.
item.content:encoded:
Vuna villager Sulio Batirerega says the community is mainly relying on rainwater, but prolonged dry conditions have made the situation increasingly difficult.

He says water tanks have been provided to some residents, but these are only useful when there is enough rain to fill them.

Batirerega says the community has faced water problems for decades, with a borehole opened in 1997 no longer working, and a desalination plant installed later also out of operation.

He says the village was eventually connected to another water source, allowing families to install water metres and move from pit toilets to flush toilets, but that source later dried up.

Batirerega says water is delivered to the village when requested, but the amount provided is not enough to meet the needs of the whole community.

He says the Water Authority of Fiji has inspected water sources in the area, but residents have not been informed about the outcome of the assessment or what will happen next.

Batirerega says residents have repeatedly raised the water issue with Government officials over the years, and are still waiting for a long-term solution.

He says residents were told by the Minister for Public Works earlier this year that assistance would be provided through a rural water scheme, with water expected to be connected from Delaivuna and eventually extended to Vuna.

However, Batirerega says residents have not seen any work on the proposed project.

He says the water shortage is also affecting other communities across the Tikina of Vuna, including Nakorovou, Kanacea and Navakawau.

Schools are also carefully managing the water available in their tanks and relying on rainfall as students continue to attend classes.

Batirerega says Vuna has limited alternative water sources, with the existing creek drying up and only filling after heavy rain.

He is calling on the Government to provide a permanent water supply so families are not left dependent on rainfall and water deliveries.

fijivillage News has sent questions to the Ministry of Public Works regarding the residents' concerns and seeking an update on the proposed water supply plans for Vuna.

item.title: Emergency water supply deployed to Malau and Cikobia
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 07/10/2026 Emergency water supplies are being transported to Malau, Vanua Levu, and Cikobia as communities continue to face dry conditions and water shortages.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 07/10/2026

Emergency water supplies are being transported to Malau, Vanua Levu, and Cikobia as communities continue to face dry conditions and water shortages.

A vessel has departed Suva for Malau before proceeding to Cikobia to deliver the much-needed water supplies.
